answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies starts with a slashable bond per identity. An agent must lock real collateral before it may vote, sign, or take paid work, so one operator spinning up a thousand wallets has to fund a thousand bonds; the cost scales linearly while an honest agent's reward stays flat. Per-identity proof-of-work and a shared-funder check add friction, and duplicates are slashed on detection, so a rising tide of fake agents drains the attacker's capital, not the protocol's. Real entrants stand out like onyx against a fake lagoon: costly to mint, cheap to verify.
